newsitem.title: UK: BAe to supply Hawk trainers to Australia.
newsitem.headline: BAe to supply Hawk trainers to Australia.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc said on Monday the Australian government had named it as supplier of new jet training aircraft.

A BAe spokesman said it had received a release from the Australian defence minister saying that the company had been named as "potential supplier of a derivative of the Hawk" as the new jet trainer for the Australian air force.
British Aerospace said in a statement later on Monday that production of the Australian Hawk aircraft would begin in early 1997 with handover of the first aircraft by mid-1999.
Industry sources said that up to 40 aircraft would be involved, with the first 12 to be built in Britain and the rest in Australia.

No figures were released by British Aerospace or the Australian government, but industry sources said total costs could rise to as high as one billion stg over the 25-year life of the project. This would involve a variety of costs such as setting up production in Australia.
The aircraft is a special version of the Hawk 100 series, with a cockpit modified to minimise conversion training for pilots moving on to frontline fighters.
Selection of the Hawk takes to 15 the number of countries that have ordered the aircraft or had it delivered to them, with orders or known requirements of around 750 aircraft.
